thread:
maria: Quick sync — I'm starting a small refactor to decouple the bench runner from the validator adapter. Goal: let teams run perf smoke locally without pulling the full golden corpus.

vijay: Nice. Is the plan to keep the validator API stable (same handshake) or introduce a versioned adapter?

maria: Versioned adapter. Minimal handshake: `ping -> capabilities -> run`. Adapter v2 will add an optional `sample_hint` field to speed up warmup.

lin: Love the minimal handshake. Two quick tradeoffs: 1) if we change response shape we need a migration layer in the runtime, 2) adding `sample_hint` risks skewing bench results if teams overopt.

kevin: For migration I'd prefer a thin shim in the admit-gateway that translates v2->v1 until we finish canary. That keeps runtime stable.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: deploy shim + feature flag. Canary on dedicated pool for 24h, then widen.

vijay: What's the acceptance criteria for widening? Latency regressions + quality delta thresholds? Specific numbers?

maria: Yup. Suggested gates: 99th p50 token latency increase < 5%, and golden-set perplexity delta < 0.5 on our eval harness. Also no more than 0.5% increase in generation failure rate.

eva: Also add telemetry for `sample_hint` usage and breakdown by model family. We should detect if clients always pass tiny hints (gaming the metric).

lin: Good call. Add an alert if >50% of runs use a hint shorter than the golden median.

kevin: On the bench side: can we support a local lightweight smoke command? e.g. `rbin bench --smoke --short` that hits adapter v2?

maria: Yes. Implementation sketch: adapter v2 accepts `smoke:true` and returns a tiny golden subset and warmup tokens. Local runner will fallback to a cached artifact if the adapter doesn't support smoke.

vijay: Fallback policy sounds important. If adapter advertises `smoke` but the response is empty, treat as adapter fault and fail-open to v1 behavior.

maria: Exactly. I'll add that to the handshake: `capabilities: {smoke: bool, hintable: bool}` and a status code enum.

onboard-bot: Note: created ticket MLON-3289 for "adapter v2 shim + canary rollout" (assignee: maria).

eva: One more thing — bench measurement variance. We need to seed RNG and fix seqlen distributions when smoke runs to reduce noise.

lin: Agree. Also capture kernel selection (quantized vs fp16) in telemetry so we can correlate perf changes to execution path.

kevin: For deployment: timeline? I can land the shim this week and schedule canary Monday. Need an ops window for dedicated pool changes.

maria: Timeline works. I'll draft the runbook: how to flip flag, rollback steps, and quick queries to run if we see failure.

vijay: Can you paste the runbook snippet here when ready? A couple of short commands would be helpful.

maria: Putting a tiny snippet below — will expand in the runbook doc.

```bash
# canary enable
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/flags -d '{"name":"adapter_v2_canary","state":"on","target":"dedicated-pool-3"}'
# quick perf check
rquery metrics 'service=bench_runner AND path=adapter_v2' --agg=percentile(99,token_latency)
# rollback
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/flags -d '{"name":"adapter_v2_canary","state":"off"}'
```

lin: Nice. Also add a smoke-check: `rbin bench --smoke --model m-mosaic-7b --seed 42` to validate deterministic warmup.

maria: Will do. Thanks all. I'll open the PR against adaptor-service and link the runbook. Planning to start the shim draft tonight.

kevin: :thumbsup:

vijay: :eyes: Keep us posted if you need reviewers for the adapter tests.

onboard-bot: Reminder scheduled: canary-check-in @maria in 24h.
